newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish shares extend surge, seen down on Tuesday.
newsitem.headline: Polish shares extend surge, seen down on Tuesday.

text.p: Polish shares rose for the sixth session running on Monday but analysts said the strong selling after price fixing signalled that last week's apparent sudden foreign buying had lead to profit-taking.

The bourse rose 3.3 percent on Monday and 10.9 percent last week in ever higher turnover but analysts saw a fall on Tuesday and said this week, shortened by Friday's Assumption Day holiday, could signficantly correct last week's surge.
"I don't see enough strong impulses that would be able to sustain such a growth trend," said Mateusz Andrzejewski, an analyst at Bank Pekao SA brokerage.
Analysts said one possible reason for last week's sudden surge, the relative attractiveness of Polish stocks after big gains in Hungary, was disappearing as Warsaw stocks rose and Budapest fell.
The Hungarian bourse fell 5.8 percent on Monday.

The main market's all-share WIG index rose 3.3 percent to 17,303.7 points and turnover inched up 1.3 percent to 308.5 million zlotys ($88.8 million) on both markets. Gainers led losers by 88 to 15 with seven stocks stable.
Analysts said the run-up to next month's parliamentary elections was another reason players might refrain from buying.
Banks continued to lead Warsaw's growth trend after previous falls with PBR up 9.9 percent in light trade and Slaski up 9.8 percent in heavy trade.
Analysts said electrode maker ZEW, which dropped 5.2 percent on Monday after a one-month suspension due to flood damage, should fall again on Tuesday. insurance compensation.
